source.title: Adversarial Weight Perturbation Improves Generalization in Graph Neural Network
source.authors: Yihan Wu; Aleksandar Bojchevski; Heng Huang

record.file_problem: Text includes the main paper and supplementary material; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extracting the relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures training-to-test generalization gaps and loss-landscape flatness in GNNs, using a different setup from the magnitude-aware sharpness comparison in V7.
record.gate_note: The study reports natural accuracy and robustness results for WT-AWP, but those metrics do not directly test the listed versions. The relevant result is its comparison of training loss landscapes and generalization gaps in Figure 10; cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flatness–generalization connection to develop a GNN regularizer. It does not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation-tolerance ranking against training–test error gaps. Its loss-landscape plots use unscaled random directions, and its defined generalization gap is a perturbed-training-loss difference, not a training–test error gap. None of V1–V8 is directly tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that WT-AWP mitigates AWP's vanishing-gradient problem and improves natural and robust GNN performance across graph learning tasks, attributing these improvements to flatter minima. The record broadly captures that conclusion, but its reference to a declining training gap should specify the paper's perturbed-loss gap rather than imply a measured training–test error gap.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses adversarial weight perturbation as a training regularizer in GNNs and compares its loss landscape and training gap; it does not use the magnitude-aware sharpness ranking method described in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported gap behavior differs between WT-AWP and AWP; WT-AWP's gap fluctuates more and decreases more slowly than AWP's. The study also notes that perturbation strength affects the gap behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.3 reports progressively flatter random-direction loss landscapes and accuracies of 83.55%, 84.21%, and 85.51% for GCN, AWP, and WT-AWP. F.6 specifies unit-normalized Gaussian directions and vertical alignment of landscapes with different final training losses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On Cora, AWP-based GCN training can produce flatter random-direction training-loss landscapes alongside higher test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: E.1 reports that WT-AWP's plotted gap fluctuates more and declines more slowly than AWP's, while still declining over time. The paper defines this gap using perturbed versus unperturbed training loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The perturbed-training-loss gap during AWP-based GCN training depends on perturbation strength and training dynamics.

record.problems: The relevant generalization-gap comparison is shown only as a plot; exact values are not stated in the text. The study uses a single GNN family and dataset for this gap comparison, and it does not test the magnitude-aware measure or comparative ranking specified in V7.
record.rows_left_out: Natural accuracy and robust accuracy tables, graph-classification accuracy, input-gradient norms, and other robustness measurements do not directly measure a listed version. Figure 5's loss-landscape and accuracy comparison does not report the training-to-test gap, so it is not included as a row.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization, including chance held-out accuracy with random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout's effect on held-out error; dropout is held fixed rather than compared.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus training–test error gaps among comparably fitted networks, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The proposed V7 limits_scope verdict is unsupported: fluctuation in the paper's sharpness-related training quantity does not qualify V7's stated correlation. Layerwise magnitude-scaled perturbation bounds used during training do not themselves constitute the magnitude-aware tolerance measurement required by V7.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers and their held-out performance.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects on test error across data regimes.

The study compares flatness and generalization in GNNs, but does not report a magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance measure or compare its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Figure 10's precise gap values are not stated in text.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: GCN
rows.operation_detail: Measured generalization gap during training; curve shown in Figure 10(b).

conditions.value: same random initialization as GCN+AWP and GCN+WT-AWP

rows.note: The text does not state the plotted gap values for this model.
rows.check: The measure is incorrectly described as a training–test generalization gap. Section 2 defines generalization gap as worst-case perturbed training loss minus unperturbed training loss; E.1 does not supply a different definition. Figure 10(b) supplies neither the magnitude-aware tolerance nor the training–test error comparison required by V7.

rows.subject: GCN+AWP
rows.operation_detail: Measured generalization gap during training; curve shown in Figure 10(b).

conditions.value: same random initialization as GCN and GCN+WT-AWP

rows.note: The text says the WT-AWP gap fluctuates more and decreases more slowly than this model's gap; exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: Figure 10(b)'s gap is not established as a training–test error gap. Its comparison with WT-AWP also changes the perturbation bound from 0.1 to 0.5. This row cannot establish V7's relationship between magnitude-aware tolerance and generalization gaps.

rows.subject: GCN+WT-AWP
rows.operation_detail: Measured generalization gap during training; curve shown in Figure 10(b).

conditions.value: same random initialization as GCN and GCN+AWP

rows.note: Text says its gap fluctuates more and decreases more slowly than GCN+AWP's, but also decreases over time.
rows.check: A declining perturbed-loss gap, with greater fluctuation and slower decline than AWP, does not show a partial V7 effect. The text attributes these dynamics to the larger perturbation bound and exploding logits; it does not measure V7's correlation.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
